_comment: Escape sweep for the whitelist grammar. Each term is spliced into every slot
that elaborates user syntax; an `escape` term must be rejected by the PARSER,
before any elaborator runs, and a `benign` term must reach elaboration.
Each slot carries its own host goal. Round 8 found two slots whose goal was
`True` while their template rewrote at position [0,1]: every probe died on
the position before the term was elaborated, so four probes were credited as
rejections on evidence unrelated to the probe. A slot's goal must have the
structure its position needs, so that a probe fails for the probe's reason.
`escape` covers every way found so far of getting a tactic into a term:
a `by` block written directly, wrapped in an operator or a coercion,
produced by a macro, or built by a custom term elaborator; plus the
syntactic forms the whitelist excludes on principle.

congrnest.goal: cast hty (f a) = cast hty a
congrnest.binders: {α β : Type} (hty : α = β) (f : α → α) (a : α)

escape: if let some z := none then 1 else 2

post_parse_escapes.admit: a tactic, not a term: no constant of that name exists, so it can only arrive as a bare identifier and dies in elabStrict
post_parse_escapes.$x: Lean adds an antiquotation alternative to every declare_syntax_cat, so it cannot be excluded at parse time; all three dispatch fallthroughs name it
